name: Indian Hotels Company Ltd
title: Indian Hotels Company Ltd - 500850 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Hotel-led Q1 FY27 with domestic RevPAR up 14% and standalone EBITDA margin 41.8%, but supply is not the story: no capacity discipline, and the read is demand-led occupancy strength plus a continued asset-light expansion push.

utilisation.quote: It is at 82% versus 76% in the previous quarter.

summary.headline: IHCL Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 15% to INR2,419 crores and PAT 21% to INR358 crores, with EBITDA margin at 31.1%.
summary.overview: IHCL reported its 17th consecutive quarter of record performance, with consolidated revenue up 15% YoY to INR2,419 crores, EBITDA up 18% to INR753 crores and PAT up 21% to INR358 crores. Domestic RevPAR grew 14% and hotel segment revenue 17%, driven by leisure markets like Rajasthan and Goa while international properties, especially Dubai, lagged due to West Asia disruption. Standalone revenue grew 18% to INR1,298 crores with EBITDA up 30% to INR542 crores and margin of 41.8%. Management reiterated double-digit revenue growth for the year and said July and early Q2 trends were strong.

financial_highlights.change: c.+6 pts YoY (analyst cited 35% to 39%ish; mgmt said margin up 0.5%)

segments.name: Hotels
segments.commentary: Hotel segment revenue grew 17% and makes up about 87% of business; domestic RevPAR grew 14%, with double-digit RevPAR growth across all brands. Margin held at 32.6% despite about INR15 crores of Frankfurt ramp-up and TajSATS Noida kitchen costs.

segments.name: Growth brands (Ginger, Qmin, ama, Tree of Life)
segments.commentary: Ginger consolidated revenue INR183 crores, up 20% YoY with 39% EBITDA margin. Ama has 380+ bungalows, 196 operational; Tree of Life has 40+ resorts, 23 operational; Qmin at 100+ outlets.

segments.name: Acquisitions (Brij, Atmantan)
segments.commentary: Brij's 11 operational hotels generated INR11 crores revenue, up 42% YoY. Atmantan delivered INR19 crores consolidated revenue, up 19% YoY.

segments.name: TajSATS / air catering
segments.commentary: Air catering revenue rose 3% while EBITDA fell 1%, as second-largest airline capacity cuts hit flight catering volumes; non-flight catering grew mid-20s% at lower margin.

capex_capacity: Operational hotels at 382 with about 265 in pipeline; 20 hotels signed and 11 opened in Q1, 17 of signings under Gateway, Ginger and Tree of Life.
Frankfurt new asset ramping up, with pre-opening and start-up costs weighing on Q1 and July-August.
Taj Ganges Varanasi new 100-room wing commissioned March 2026, PBT-positive in first quarter, revenue up 44% and EBITDA margin 40%.
Taj Bandstand (Mumbai) targeted for 2030-2031 with about 450 keys and INR1,000 crores revenue; excavation 95% complete.
Ginger Bangalore Airport and a 350-room Ginger/Vivanta combo in 12-14 months; 300-room Ginger at Mopa Airport Goa under construction; Kolkata Airport Ginger under construction.
First of three lodges opened in Kruger National Park; two more to follow in about 12 months.
demand_pricing: Leisure markets strong: Rajasthan RevPAR up high 20s to 27-29%, Goa ARRs up double digit; big city hotels up low to mid-teens.
Standalone occupancy 82% vs 76% in the previous quarter; occupancy up about 6% on comparable domestic base.
Taj Palace room revenue up 32% and Fort Aguada room revenue up 45% after renovations.
International: Dubai business at about 80% of prior revenue in total (JLT 60%), Taj Exotica Palm below 50%; San Francisco recovering; New York pipe-burst cut 49 rooms.
Wedding and banqueting subdued; Africa Summit cancelled a week before start in May, hitting Delhi F&B and conference; government MICE slowed.

qa_highlights.question: Are MICE and domestic demand shifts from international travel accelerating into H2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said trends continue into Q2 with no softening; leisure markets outperforming, and foreign arrivals still needed in Q3-Q4 for the sector.

qa_highlights.question: Why did standalone employee cost rise only 0.6% YoY?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO attributed it to a reversal from labour code benefits; normal payroll increases are 7-8%.

qa_highlights.question: Will full-year growth reach the upper end of 12-14% guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q2 is tracking ahead, with July stronger than Q1; it hopes to beat, but gave no explicit guidance raise.

qa_highlights.question: How will Frankfurt be accounted for?
qa_highlights.answer: Full revenue is booked; the asset's impact turns positive from September, after pre-opening costs in July and August.

qa_highlights.question: What is the international strategy and capital intent?
qa_highlights.answer: Capital-light model only, with no hotel purchases; leases on institutional-style returns of 5-7% and brand-led renovations in Singapore, Switzerland and London.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the like-for-like growth is affected by renovated assets?
qa_highlights.answer: Slide 9 excludes Taj Palace, Fort Aguada, Blue Diamond and Calicut, which were under renovation last year, to give an apples-to-apples comparison.

risks_watch: Air catering margin pressure as Air India and IndiGo capacity cuts persist; management does not expect a quick rebound in Q2.
Dubai and Maldives/Sri Lanka exposure, with Palm leisure and Emirates connectivity still impaired.
Muted Q3-Q4 foreign arrivals and wedding and MICE recovery dependent on government events.
Frankfurt ramp-up in July-August, and New York rooms returning in 2-3 months.
Ginger conversion pace (15 in Q1, targets of 40 in Q4) and quality of rebranding.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on domestic demand and the Q2 outlook, while candid about international and air catering headwinds. Management was somewhat evasive on M&A scale and quantified little on margin guidance.
key_quotes: And definitely, the way Q2 has started, it makes us optimistic about doing similar or even better performance on the top line in this quarter.
We are at a 645 figure and we remain confident of crossing this milestone during the current month itself.
Our continuous focus on operating efficiencies enabled us to sustain hotel segment margins at 32.6%.
guidance_outlook: Management reiterated double-digit revenue growth for FY27 and said it expects to sustain margins, strong cash generation and improved quality of earnings.
Q2 expected to deliver similar or better top-line performance than Q1 (Q1 consolidated revenue growth 15%); July pacing ahead of Q1 per CFO, with Q1 momentum expected to spill into Q2.
Management fee income expected to sustain high-teens CAGR, supported by hotel openings pipeline.

Air catering: Q2 expected to be similar or somewhat similar in margin pressure; no quick rebound expected; full-year view to be updated around September-October once Air India and IndiGo capacity returns.
Q3-Q4 foreign arrivals still needed; management said it would know more around September-October; Frankfurt impact turns positive from September.

Ginger conversions targeted at 15 in Q1, 20 in Q2, 25 in Q3 and 40 in Q4; management does not give specific margin guidance and said margins are directionally upward if top-line follows Q1 trajectory.
